item.title: Sagar Defence, Encube Ethicals among 4 firms to secure Sebi's nod for IPOs
item.description: Sagar Defence Engineering, Encube Ethicals, Arjun Jewellers and IFL Finance have received Sebi's approval to launch IPOs, with proposed issues including fresh shares and offers for sale.
item.dc:creator: Press Trust of India
item.content:encoded: Sagar Defence, Encube Ethicals among 4 cos to secure Sebi's nod for IPOs New Delhi, Nov 6 (PTI) Four companies, including Sagar Defence Engineering Ltd and specialty pharmaceutical firm Encube Ethicals, have received approval from Sebi to launch their initial public offerings (IPOs), paving the way for their proposed public issues. According to a Sebi update on Friday, jewellery retailer Arjun Jewellers and gold loan-focused non-banking financial company (NBFC) IFL Finance have also received the market regulator's approval. These four companies, which filed their preliminary papers between July and August 1, received SEBI's observations between October 21 and November 4. Sagar Defence Engineering received observations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on November 4. The company had filed its draft papers through the confidential pre-filing route. The IPO size is estimated at around Rs 3,000 crore, according to people familiar with the matter. Encube Ethicals' proposed Rs 3,000-crore IPO is entirely an offer for sale (OFS) by promoter Mehul Madhusudan Shah and existing shareholder Frontier Investment Holdings Pte Ltd. Since the issue is entirely an OFS, the company will not receive any proceeds from the public offering, with the entire amount going to the selling shareholders. Sebi also approved the IPO of Arjun Jewellers on November 4. The company's proposed public issue comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 200 crore, with no OFS component. Additionally, IFL Finance's proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to 3.55 crore equity shares and an OFS of up to 30 lakh shares by existing shareholders. The New Delhi-based non-deposit-taking NBFC plans to utilise the proceeds from the fresh issue to augment its Tier-I capital base to support future capital requirements, including lending activities, and meet capital adequacy norms. All four companies will be listed on the BSE and NSE.

item.description: The rupee gained 0.60 per cent to close at 93.91 against the dollar on Friday, its highest level since April 22, supported by falling crude oil prices and foreign equity inflows ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Economy / News / Rupee hits six-month high of 93.91 against dollar on oil price decline

Rupee hits six-month high of 93.91 against dollar on oil price decline The rupee gained 0.60 per cent to close at 93.91 against the dollar on Friday, its highest level since April 22, supported by falling crude oil prices and foreign equity inflows

The Indian rupee strengthened to a six-month high of 93.91 against the dollar, supported by lower crude oil prices and foreign inflows into domestic equities. Image: Bloomberg

Aathira Varier Mumbai 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 06 2026 | 6:07 PM IST

Listen to This Article

The Indian rupee gained for the sixth consecutive day, rising to a six-month high of 93.91 against the dollar, driven by lower crude oil prices and higher foreign inflows into the domestic equity market over the past week, according to dealers. It was the best-performing Asian currency during the month.   The rupee, which opened at 94.49 against the dollar, compared with the previous close of 94.47, strengthened to 93.83 during the day before giving up some gains to settle at 93.91, its strongest level since April 22, 2026.   The currency, which was the second-best-performing Asian currency in October 2026 after the South Korean won, became the best-performing Asian currency on Friday. It was also the best-performing Asian currency in November, driven by week-long gains.

The rupee's 0.60 per cent gain on Friday was its biggest single-day rise since October 12, 2026, when the currency gained 0.99 per cent.   “The Indian Rupee outpaced all of Asian peers, scoring its biggest single-day surge since October 12 to hit a six-month peak. Fueled by heavy foreign inflows and sliding crude prices, market sentiment went into overdrive amid a parabolic rally in domestic equities sparked by the buzz around the "Anti-AI" trade and ease of geopolitical uncertainties,” said Dilip Parmar, research analyst, HDFC Securities. The Indian equity markets, driven by foreign inflows, were at a nine-month high on Friday.   “In the near term, spot USDINR is expected to head south with support pegged at 93.50 and resistance ticking up to 94.30,” he added.

The January 2027 Brent contract was also down at $96.84 per barrel on Friday, compared with $98.29 per barrel on Thursday. Prices have fallen from $117.64 per barrel on October 30, 2026, following reports of diplomatic engagement between the US and Iran, followed by the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections. Crude prices in the spot market also traded at $96.07 per barrel, lower than $98.69 per barrel on Thursday.   “Global crude benchmark Brent oil experienced massive two-way volatility on Friday, reversing sharply from early highs to drop to $97.311 per barrel after failing to sustain a breakout above the psychological $100 mark,” according to a report by Finrex Treasury Advisors.

India’s foreign exchange reserves fell for the eighth consecutive week to $717.06 billion in the week ended October 30, 2026, due to a decline in foreign currency assets. While total reserves fell by $2.7 billion, foreign currency assets declined by $2.09 billion. Gold reserves fell by $559 million.   After hitting an all-time high of $785.7 billion in the week ended September 4, 2026, total foreign exchange reserves fell by $68.7 billion over the next eight weeks as the central bank sold dollars in the foreign exchange market to curb volatility.   The yield on the 10-year benchmark government bond rose by 2 basis points (bps) to end at 7.19 per cent on Friday, recovering from Thursday’s close of 7.17 per cent, its lowest level since September 29, 2026, tracking gains in crude oil prices from the day’s lows and the results of government bond auctions. It is down 22 bps during the month and up 16 bps so far in FY27 and 60 bps in the calendar year.

item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / News / SP Group's Eqyizen plans to raise up to $200 mn via rupee bonds: Bankers

SP Group's Eqyizen plans to raise up to $200 mn via rupee bonds: Bankers The Shapoorji Pallonji Group unit plans to issue zero-coupon rupee-denominated bonds maturing in July 2029, with the fundraising expected to be completed by the end of November, bankers said

Bankers said some of the company's approved borrowing limit remains unutilised and it wants to reach its fundraising target | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 06 2026 | 3:58 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India's Eqyizen Investment, a unit of Shapoorji Pallonji Group, plans to raise around $150 million to $200 million of rupee equivalent funds through the sale of zero-coupon rupee-denominated bonds maturing in July 2029, two bankers said on Friday. "The company will finalise the quantum that it intends to borrow in rupee terms and should be done with the issuance before end of November," one of the bankers mentioned above said. The bankers spoke on the condition of anonymity, while the Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. Bankers said some of the company's approved borrowing limit remains unutilised and it wants to reach its fundraising target.   In October, Eqyizen Investment had raised around ₹4,450 crore (about $473 million) through a similar debt issuance at a yield of 18.95%, after raising around ₹21,350 crore via another issue at the same yield in July. In both these instances, Mercury Finance, another SP Group firm, had raised funds through zero-coupon US dollar-denominated bonds due July 2029 and invested the proceeds in rupee securities of Eqyizen. The outlook for the real estate conglomerate's bonds has improved after Tata Trusts, Tata Sons' controlling shareholder, said that SP Group had proposed a plan to sell ₹25,000 crore worth of its stake in Tata Sons. The proposal has yet to move forward amid differences between Tata Trusts and Tata Sons.

item.title: RBI proposes ₹100 crore limit on bank loans for agri infrastructure
item.description: The RBI has proposed a ₹100 crore aggregate loan limit per borrower for agricultural infrastructure under revised priority sector lending norms.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / Banking / RBI proposes ₹100 crore limit on bank loans for agri infrastructure

RBI proposes ₹100 crore limit on bank loans for agri infrastructure The RBI has proposed a ₹100 crore aggregate loan limit per borrower for agricultural infrastructure under revised priority sector lending norms.

The Reserve Bank of India has proposed revised priority sector lending norms, including a ₹100 crore aggregate loan limit per borrower for agricultural infrastructure and higher eligibility limits for education and renewable energy loans. (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 05 2026 | 11:16 PM IST

Listen to This Article

The Reserve Bank on Thursday proposed that loans for agricultural infrastructure will be subject to an aggregate sanctioned limit of Rs 100 crore per borrower from the banking system. As part of the ongoing effort towards consolidation of various instructions, the Reserve Bank of India said it has undertaken a review of the extant guidelines relating to Priority Sector Lending (PSL) and proposes to issue directions on the subject for different regulated entities, including commercial banks and regional rural banks. A draft direction on commercial banks proposed an aggregate loan limit of Rs 4 crore per borrowing entity for crop loans, medium and long-term loans for agriculture and allied activities, as well as loans for pre- and post-harvest activities.   It also said: "Loans for agriculture infrastructure will be subject to an aggregate sanctioned limit of Rs 100 crore per borrower from the banking system."   The lending to the agriculture sector will include farm credit (agriculture and allied activities), lending for agriculture infrastructure and ancillary activities. The draft further said that loans to individuals for educational purposes, including vocational courses, not exceeding Rs 25 lakh, will be considered as eligible for priority sector classification. Also Read

RBI tightens cyber oversight of non-bank payment system operators

RBI forms panel for consultation on financial markets, emerging risks

RBI forms financial markets consultative panel headed by Dy Guv Rohit Jain

Regarding renewable energy, it said bank loans up to a limit of Rs 35 crore to borrowers for renewable energy-based power generators and for renewable energy-based public utilities -- street lighting systems, remote village electrification -- will be eligible for priority sector classification. For individual households, the loan limit will be Rs 10 lakh per borrower, the draft said. Agriculture, MSMEs, exports, education, housing, social infrastructure, and renewable energy are among the categories under the priority sector. The RBI has also issued separate draft directions for small finance banks, local area banks, and regional rural banks. RBI has invited comments and feedback on the drafts by November 26.
